# Assembled prompt editing

`make linux-prompt-test` now runs the native assembled application in four private sessions, followed by the existing native prompt-editor owner. Minimum 420×520 dark, narrow 480×640 light, wide 1060×780 dark and malformed-configuration 480×640 dark cover **53 states and fourteen complete-window images**. Every scenario launches a separate process to reopen its saved files. The [independent fixture](released-application-prompts.json), SHA-256 `82bc13d3872ca44251db55bfd9407cdfe1ba9f9de11389d965a43cad5ef48a90`, records unchanged v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. A focused replay is `bash linux/tests/run_application_smoke.sh prompts wide`.

The external reference observer verifies all 77 released modules before activation and imported module paths/digests after shutdown. It invokes the actual application, registered actions, private keyboard/pointer events, buttons, dialogs and buffers. No application handler or service is replaced. The collector remains under ignored `tmp/`; native Make consumes static observations and native external peers. The wide scenario owns the full interaction flow; the other three retain distinct size/theme/configuration and restart contracts without duplicating the recording flow.

| Retired contract | Native observation and retained owner |
| --- | --- |
| Empty, hovered and keyboard-focused prompt gear | Empty Polish stays disabled while its gear opens; real private pointer movement changes gear visibility; focused Space opens the editor and produces no provider turn |
| Ctrl+P and template/style entry points | Real command keys select the exact catalog title; all five Live gears preserve template selection; a style created through the actual Save prompt dialog opens from commands, settings and its menu |
| Save, Cancel, reset and conflict | Actual controls preserve Markdown/Unicode bytes and private file modes, retain or discard edits, stage/reset defaults and refuse an external disk conflict |
| Restart and malformed configuration | Four second processes reopen the persisted override and compare controls/layout; malformed configuration bytes remain unchanged in both processes |
| Instructions during recording | Two real PCM captures and observed provider requests preserve the old instructions through pause/resume and manual draft editing; the next capture uses the saved instructions |
| Saved-style disk edits | The real menu execution resolves changed on-disk instructions and saves the actual provider response as a conversation reply |
| Incognito | The real setting rejects prompt writes; saved privacy on restart disables the six workspace actions and displays the released notice |
| Validation, damaged files and competing editors | The existing native `prompt_editor` owner retains its 81 observations, including empty/oversized text, invalid UTF-8, stale privacy, custom baselines and retention of an already-open draft |

The wide flow records two exact speech HTTP requests and four complete Codex turns. A real external response gate holds the resumed Live request while the edited Architecture draft is observed; cancellation reaps that provider. The next capture uses `Next recording instructions`, and saved-style execution uses `External style instructions`. Other scenarios and all restarts permit no HTTP request or Codex turn. PCM input is stored as one repeated sample block; expansion preserves the independently recorded WAV byte count and digest. The clipboard stays exactly `untouched prompt clipboard`. A fixed synthetic History input supplies its identifier/date; resulting writes are observed rather than injected.

Only the generated custom-style UUID is normalized to `$STYLE` in labels and filenames. Prompt text, requests, documents, replies, configuration-error state and control sensitivity remain exact. The private runner mounts its own `/tmp`; a stable `/tmp/mluva-prompt-comparison` symlink points to persistent evidence beneath that session. This preserves the real displayed file path in both applications without masking pixels. Restart checks require that alias and a different saved process ID.

The comparison exposed a native startup bug: when Incognito was already saved, the workspace loaded its configuration without initializing its separate privacy state. Title, continuation, Polish, Structure, Save prompt and Rewrite controls remained available after reopening, and the privacy notice differed. The production fix initializes workspace privacy before loading the latest conversation. Capture-time frozen privacy remains owned by the existing capture controller. This is an observed UI initialization regression; the check does not establish a backend data leak.

The initial full-window restart comparison exposed that difference. A fresh unchanged-release observation then pinned all six controls and the notice; the native assertion failed before the fix with all six values true instead of false (`tmp/native-prompts-privacy-before.log`). After the one-line repair, all 53 states and fourteen layouts pass. The earlier visual diagnostic and difference image remain in `tmp/native-prompts-first-make-pixels-diagnostic.log` and `tmp/native-prompts-restart-diff.png`.

All fourteen final images have zero differing pixels without masks (`tmp/native-prompts-final-pixels.log`). Native captures are `tmp/application/run.rK4PGQ/{minimum,narrow,wide,bad-config}/session.*/native-application-prompts{,-reopen}/`. Final reference logs are `tmp/native-prompts-controls-source-{minimum,narrow,wide,bad-config}.log`, with private sessions `ZVtkYx`, `bG1dRL`, `OBB3GM` and `RHHaa0` respectively. The complete X11 surfaces include ten additional pixels per dimension around the specified client allocations. Visual inspection checked the minimum editor and the repaired wide restart.

The old Make route fails at a positively verified interpreter trap (`tmp/native-prompts-before.log`). Actual final native Make passes all four first/reopen pairs and the existing editor owner while `/usr/bin/python3` and `uv` are blocked; neither trap is used (`tmp/native-prompts-final-make.log`, outer `session.n4BMWb`, editor `tmp/application/run.l8uqJ5/session.dWptfX/`). The obsolete 339-line `prompt_editor_smoke.py` and its Make prerequisite are retired. Its substituted callbacks and manually assigned Live state are replaced by real external operations; shared rendering helpers retain their other consumers.

The default assembled application still passes fifteen workflows/147 states and the command/settings owner (`tmp/native-prompts-final-siblings.log`, `tmp/application/run.OPt0Pi/session.NpEJMA/`). A scratch sibling wrapper initially used the wrong guarded PATH for preferences and stopped before exercising that suite. After correcting that wrapper, the remaining checks pass seventeen preference transactions/132 states, 26 Live transactions/122 states, and seventeen screenshot workflows/79 states plus storage/cancellation faults (`tmp/native-prompts-final-siblings-corrected.log`). No application fix was made for the wrapper error.

Final actual `make test` passes 139 tests, zero failures and 68 ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy configurations, formatting and generated-document consistency. Relevant ignored desktop checks run explicitly above. Actual `make linux-python-test` passes 571 tests plus Ruff/formatting for 152 remaining files. Full ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Logs are `tmp/native-prompts-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-prompts-final-python.log` and `tmp/native-prompts-final-gates.log`; the private gate session is `tmp/native-prompts-final-gates-evidence/session.Gd0icD/`. Existing narrow GtkText and PyGObject warnings remain recorded. No hosted or paid CI is used.

Substantial review separates production **+1/−0**, Make/runner tooling **+21/−11**, tests/support **+663/−350** (including the retired Python helper), and the independent fixture **3,531 lines/184,715 bytes**. Documentation is separate. The new 581-line observer shares the existing assembled application and shutdown owner, adds no production test API and keeps exhaustive component variants at their existing owner.

The environment uses private X11/Openbox, GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2, Libadwaita 1.9.3, scale 1, disabled animations/cursor blinking and software Mesa. HOME/XDG, clipboard, buses, network/PID/mount namespaces are isolated; physical devices and the system bus are masked. No host input, credentials, microphone, user content or installed files are used. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0, and the three-model lineup with Qwen3-ASR 1.7B as default is unchanged. Complete joined workflows, page-driven provisioning, remaining Python/tooling removal, clean distribution, platform/device checks and current performance acceptance remain open. Every whole-workflow matrix row stays Pending.
